summary.headline: Pennar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR1,029.25 crore, a first quarterly crossing of INR1,000 crore, with PBT up 24.3% to INR50.9 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time in a quarter, with EBITDA up 21.6% to INR114.8 crore and PBT margin at 5.01% versus 4.52% a year ago. Sequential gross margin softened on raw material inflation, which management calls temporary, and ROCE of 20% and ROE of about 11.7% were described as unsatisfactory. Order backlog is strong across PEB India (about INR1,008 crore), PEB US ($93.1 million) and Boilers (INR152 crore), though India PEB execution and the hydraulics backlog (INR35 crore) remain weak spots. PAT was lower than PBT suggests because of a prior-year one-time tax adjustment of INR1.8 crore.

segments.name: Custom Design Building Solutions (PEB India, PEB US, Telco, Ascent)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 21% YoY from INR465 crore to INR563 crore and 11% QoQ. Order backlog is about INR1,008 crore in India and $93.1 million in the US; US split is Ascent 62 and structurals 31 (in $ million), with about 50% of Ascent structurals backlog tied to data centers.

segments.name: Diversified Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR467.9 crore, flat YoY against INR468.3 crore, and up 21.5% QoQ from INR385.3 crore in Q1 FY27. Around 30% of the segment is legacy railways and related businesses.

segments.name: Body-in-White (BIW)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 of hot stamping capex is complete and the LP2 status with Hyundai is achieved, with production to start within weeks. Phase 2 of hot stamping and cold stamping is due by March 2027, and new orders from Hyundai, Sears and TIVOLT were noted.

segments.name: Engineering Services (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 36.5% YoY, the strongest quarter for the business to date, with higher-margin status cited by management.

segments.name: Boilers
segments.commentary: Order backlog is INR152 crore, including a retrofit and revamping order for pressure parts for TPH or PFBC boilers and the first pressure vessel orders.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog is INR35 crore. Management says US policy uncertainty is weighing and the business needs patience.

segments.name: Tech Pennar
segments.commentary: Management says the business is stabilising, with its customer base widening across Europe and the US and Australia newly opened.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin: management expects H2 margin stability with no repeat of the sharp Q1-Q2 raw material spike, and says the inflation rate is moderating.
Long-term PBT margin target of 7%; management is committing to reaching it in the medium term, having moved from about 3% two to two-and-a-half years ago to about 5% now.
Management guides to a substantial high-double-digit growth in full-year profitability (PBT) and says H2 revenue and profit should be substantially higher than H1.
BIW and boilers are guided to very high double-digit growth over the next couple of quarters; Q4 revenue is expected to rise on new orders and new capacity.
Compensation increases of 10-15% for FY27 overall, with a lower increase expected next year.
Management targets ROCE above 20%, possibly 25%, and ROE of 15%; the stated ambition is INR10,000 crore revenue by FY30 (AGM statement), with the company saying it is tracking above that plan.
capex_capacity: BIW hot stamping phase 1 complete; LP2 status with Hyundai achieved; production for both projects to start over the next few weeks.
BIW phase 2 hot stamping and cold stamping capex is expected to complete by March 2027.
Boiler capacity augmentation is planned, with AFBC, RG, DG grade and CFBC chosen as core technologies; management says current capacity is not yet at peak utilisation in PEB India.
Company bought the US leasehold land previously held in a subsidiary under ROU; PP&E rose INR48.68 crore to INR986.2 crore, and INR201 crore was invested during the period.
Management intends to keep adding capacity in a capital-efficient manner, with ROCE as the gate for capital additions.
demand_pricing: PEB India order book about INR1,008 crore, described as sustained above INR1,000 crore after crossing that level last quarter.
US order backlog $93.1 million (about $93 million), with the company saying it has seen no decline in data center orders.
Price variation clauses now cover all order backlogs, protecting gross contribution value in rupee terms, but preserving percentage margin requires renegotiation.
Raw material pricing: quarterly pricing from some major steel producers (JSW cited) and order-level vendor price locks for the medium term.
Management says the market-share goal is 5-10% in each business; it does not expect cannibalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined over the last two quarters, and what protects against raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline mainly to RM price inflation in Q1 and Q2, which it says is now moderating. Protection comes from PVC clauses on all backlog, quarterly steel pricing and vendor price locks at order booking, though timing lags can cause slight quarterly margin dips.

qa_highlights.question: How much will employee expenses rise going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Salaries were up 21% YoY, driven by SM Structural in the consolidated base and a standalone workmen's salary revision that occurs once every three years. Management says FY27 compensation rises of 10-15% are expected and the increase will be much lower next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new US politics affect the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no decline in the addressable market or order backlog, and that data center orders in India and the US have held up, with Texas cited as about 40% of US data center build.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables are growing faster than sales; is there a collection problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AR days rose about 4 days and called it temporary. It argued that customer advances, which rose in other current liabilities, should be netted against receivables, and said there is no receivable problem and provisioning is in place.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cycle time for converting the US backlog into revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ascent takes about 6 months on average, ranging from 3 months for GC warehouse work to 9 months, with data center work at the longer end.

qa_highlights.question: Why has BIW not grown in line with the Stellantis-to-Hyundai expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Stellantis offtake was lower than expected. It expects Hyundai programmes, which are higher volume and domestic rather than export, to lift BIW revenue sharply over the next two quarters, and new OEM onboarding takes about 1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans and timelines for the legacy businesses (steel, railways, tubes)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy revenue declined this quarter and it expects no further sequential decline, with stability or moderate growth ahead. It said the Board is evaluating options and more detail will come over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no investor presentation this quarter, and when will segment EBITDA and ROCE be reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the presentation was withheld to build a new format that includes segment revenue, EBIT and capital employed (ROCE). Segment ROCE will be reported with consistent cost and capital allocation, with the new format expected next quarter.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: H2 gross margin stability depends on price variation clauses, quarterly steel pricing and vendor price locks working as management describes.
Working capital is elevated: inventory was built for the record backlog, receivables rose, and management targets faster inventory turns and collections in H2.
ROCE of 20% and ROE of about 11.7% are below management's own target. Low utilisation in India PEB, and the hydraulics and legacy businesses, are drags on capital efficiency.
Hydraulics: US policy uncertainty has weakened the backlog (INR35 crore), and the company says recovery will take patience.
Employee costs grew 20% YoY, and the 10-15% compensation increase is a further cost pressure in FY27.
Legacy businesses (steel, railways, tubes; about INR1,300 crore gross sales) are declining and their strategic direction is still undecided.
Segmental EBITDA and ROCE disclosure has been deferred one quarter, and the investor presentation was not published this quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order backlog, revenue growth and the 7% PBT target, but candid and cautious on ROCE, working capital and the legacy businesses. Several answers were deferred to IR, and the segment reporting change was explained with a request for one more quarter of patience.
